topPRs.title: feat(template): add OPCMUpgradeV900
topPRs.author: ZakAyesh
topPRs.body:
Adds `OPCMUpgradeV900`, the upgrade half of the v9 (interop) release: it calls `OPContractsManagerV2.upgradeSuperchain` once, then `upgrade` per chain, so a set of chains already on op-contracts/v8 steps onto the v9 OPCM.

**Ordering:** this task runs before the `OPCMMigrateV900` task in #1582. `migrate` requires every chain to already be on the v9 OPCM.

Differences from `OPCMUpgradeV800`, all driven by the v9 OPCM:
- The only permitted upgrade instruction is `overrides.cfg.startingRespectedGameType`; the `startingAnchorRoot` override is rejected, so the anchor-root inputs are gone and the super-root anchor is carried forward. `_validate` asserts the respected game type landed and the anchor was not cleared.
- Version gate accepts any 9.x and checks `isPermittedUpgradeSequence` per chain.
- SUPER_CANNON_KONA is enabled when the factory already carries it (v8 cleared the CANNON_KONA impl it used to key off).
- `Challenger` is read with a tolerant lookup: super-game-only chains register none.

**Example task and simulation.** `sep/045-opcm-upgrade-v900` (Unichain Sepolia + OP Sepolia) simulates against the throwaway v9 OPCM (9.0.5) Andrea deployed on Sepolia on 2026-10-22 for template testing (`0xe09c417496c786abffefa676da9e11aab2c32ea9`, not an rc, no tag, no registry entry). The simulation passes end to end at fork block 11999987 with no validator errors for either chain. A real task must point at the released v9 OPCM. The example is not skipped in `simulate-all-templates`, so CI depends on that throwaway contract staying deployed; happy to add a skip like #1582 if preferred.

Setup tests: `test/template/OPCMUpgradeV900Setup.t.sol` (5 tests, Sepolia fork).

Open for review: the prestate in the example is the chains' current SUPER_CANNON_KONA prestate as a placeholder, and the ZK game path is unsupported as in V800.

topPRs.title: sep/110 + eth/074: Unichain SystemConfig owner to Foundation Upgrade Safe
topPRs.author: Wazabie
topPRs.body:
Transfers ownership of the Unichain Sepolia and Unichain Mainnet `SystemConfigProxy` from the Unichain SystemConfig owner Safes to the Foundation Upgrade Safe, ahead of the Unichain migration cutovers. 

Each task is a single `SystemConfig.transferOwnership(address)` call executed by the current owner: `0x325B777f8F0bC71fb6b617Bc41A8703CA7077891` on Sepolia and `0x9245d5D10AA8a842B31530De71EA86c0760Ca1b1` on Mainnet.

Both tasks use the `TransferSystemConfigOwnership` template (used already for tasks eth/065 and sep/104 - Ink transfer) with `safeAddressString = "SystemConfigOwner"` so the signer is the owner discovered on chain.

topPRs.title: ci: check out over HTTPS with a GitHub App token
topPRs.author: falcorocks
topPRs.body:
## Summary
- Add a `github-checkout` command that clones the repo over HTTPS. When the `github-checkout-app-superchain-ops` context is available and `openssl`, `curl` and `jq` are present, it mints a short-lived GitHub App installation token scoped to this repository with `contents: read` and passes it to git for the checkout step via GIT_CONFIG_* (covering fetches and lazy blob fetches); otherwise it clones anonymously.
- Add a local `checkout-with-mise` command with the same parameters as the orb command, using `github-checkout` followed by `utils/install-mise`.
- Replace the built-in `checkout` step and every `utils/checkout-with-mise` use with the new commands, and add the `github-checkout-app-superchain-ops` context to the workflow jobs that check out with the App token (jobs without it clone anonymously).

topPRs.title: ci: speed up template_regression_tests
topPRs.author: geoknee
topPRs.body:
## Why

`template_regression_tests` is the critical path of the `main` workflow (job p50 397s vs workflow p50 398s on `main`). Its single step (~389s) spends roughly:

- ~~**~100s** in `forge install`~~ **Corrected:** I'd estimated this from `forge_build`, and it was wrong. #1608, which only adds the shallow clone, ran in 390s against main's p50 of 397s. The full-history clone costs at most ~10s, which is within noise.
- **~70s** in a cold solc compile (223 files; same as `forge_build`'s `Solc 0.8.15 finished in 69.88s`).
- **~220s** simulating the 36 example fixtures in lockstep batches of 7, each batch blocked on its slowest member; 36 = 5×7 + 1, so the final fixture runs alone.

## What

No coverage change: the same 36 fixtures and the same template-to-fixture check.

- `init-submodules-shallow`: `git submodule update --init --recursive --depth 1 --jobs 8`. Nothing in the repo reads submodule history.
- `restore-forge-artifacts` / `save-forge-artifacts`: caches `out/` + `cache/`, keyed on `git ls-files -s` of every `.sol`, `foundry.toml`, `mise.toml`, and the submodule gitlinks, with a prefix fallback. Foundry's cache is content-hashed: locally, touching every `.sol` and rebuilding prints `No files changed, compilation skipped`. The cache is saved before simulating, so a flaky simulation still keeps a warm build. `forge_build` still compiles from scratch, so the clean-build check is unchanged.
- `simulate-all-templates`: replaces the fixed batches with an `xargs -0 -P 7` rolling pool (same concurrency cap). Each fixture logs `Simulated <task> in Ns`; a failure logs `FAILED: <task>` and the recipe exits non-zero after the rest finish.

## Testing

- Ran the recipe locally with `simulate-task.sh` swapped for a stub: all 36 fixtures dispatched with the correct nested-safe names and networks; a forced failure exited non-zero and named the fixture; 36 × 2s stubs finished in 13s, so the pool keeps 7 slots busy.
- `shellcheck` is clean on the recipe body.
- I couldn't run the real simulations locally (they need the CI archive RPCs) or `circleci config validate` (the private orb doesn't resolve). **CI on this PR is the real check**; the first run will be a cache miss, a re-run should show the warm-cache time.

## Possible follow-ups (not in this PR)

- `forge_test` (~248s) becomes the critical path. It also compiles cold, so the artifact cache applies.
- 31 of the 36 fixtures are already simulated by `test/tasks/Regression.t.sol` (same `multisigTask.simulate`, plus exact calldata and data-to-sign checks). The shell loop could keep only the 5 fixtures that test doesn't cover (`eth/010`, `opsep/001`, `sep/010`, `sep/034-update-fee-vault-recipient`, `sep/035-opcm-upgrade-v800`), plus one representative each for single, nested, stacked (`DEPENDS_ON`) and opsep. That's a coverage call for the owners.

topPRs.title: ci: shallow-clone submodules in template_regression_tests
topPRs.author: geoknee
topPRs.body:
## Why

`template_regression_tests` never runs `just install`, so its `forge build` auto-runs `forge install`. That clones every submodule recursively with full history, and `lib/optimism` is the entire monorepo. The job sets the pace for the whole `main` workflow (p50 397s).

## What

Adds an `init-submodules-shallow` command, `git submodule update --init --recursive --depth 1 --jobs 8`, and runs it before the simulation step. Nothing in the repo reads submodule history. This PR does nothing else, so its CI run measures the shallow clone on its own.

Split out from #1607, which also adds a forge artifact cache and a rolling simulation pool. #1607 still contains this same hunk; once this PR merges, its rebase is trivial. In #1607's first CI run the shallow init step took 26s.

## Result

**The saving is negligible.** This PR's `template_regression_tests` took 390s (shallow init 31s, simulate step 349s), against main's p50 of 397s and p95 of 566s. That's one sample, and the difference is within noise. The shallow clone is a cleanup, not a speedup. The real wins in #1607 come from the rolling pool and the artifact cache.

## Testing

- Locally, a shallow `git submodule update --init --recursive --depth 1` from a fresh worktree checked out every submodule (142MB in `lib/`), and `forge build` compiled successfully against it.
- CI on this PR is the real check: compare this job's duration with the `main` p50 of 397s.
